adjudication_note:
The 50 partial headings clustered into two classes, and only one of them is a dictionary gap. Class one is genuine vocabulary the registry never had: FIF, títulos de renda fixa, títulos públicos, desvio padrão amostral/populacional, valor futuro. Class two is heading furniture — serial numerals (`Gestão de Carteiras de Renda Fixa I / 2 / II`), chapter citations (`(Cap. V)`), and ordinary modifiers (`Principais`, `Fundamentos`, `Outras`). Widening the furniture list to absorb class two is how a coverage number gets gamed, and this campaign already had that caught once, so class two is left partial and counts against the score.

Admission rule applied to class one, because the metric reads headings and the temptation is to register headings as terms until the metric agrees with itself: a phrase is admitted only when the concept is independently attested — already in the registry, or defined in the corpus prose — never when it merely appears as a heading. Two candidates were REFUSED under it. Bare `RF` has 22 corpus occurrences and every one is inside a heading, never in a sentence, so registering it as an abbreviation of `renda fixa` would be inventing vocabulary to satisfy the instrument; the full section phrases are registered instead, in amendment 60. `títulos híbridos` appears exactly once, as the heading `Títulos Híbridos: Exemplo de Cálculo`, with no prose defining it — a real financial concept, but not one this corpus attests, so its heading stays partial.

A thirteenth concept was drafted and withdrawn before it shipped. `technical.reprisk_index` collided with `technical.rep_risk_index`, which the registry already held: the first import printed `demoted_to_review: [technical.rep_risk_index.en:RepRisk, technical.reprisk_index.en:RepRisk]`, the collision demoter doing exactly its job — two concepts claiming one surface, so both lose it. Shipping it would have cost the incumbent its automatic `RepRisk` form to buy a duplicate. The `RepRisk Index` surface is added to the incumbent in amendment 60 instead. Reading the demoter's output rather than the exit code is what caught it.

concepts.def: The CVM 175 category covering funds whose portfolio is financial assets, as opposed to the receivables and real-estate categories in the other annexes.
A debt instrument paying interest on a defined schedule, whose return is known at issue up to credit and reinvestment risk.
Debt issued by the federal government, carrying the sovereign's credit rather than a company's.
The square root of the sample variance, dividing by n minus one to correct the bias of estimating a population from a draw.
The square root of the population variance, dividing by n because every member of the set is observed.
What a sum becomes after compounding forward at a given rate for a given term.
The pooled, publicly offered, daily-priced vehicle the material contrasts with hedge funds when comparing mandates and liquidity.
Facts not yet disclosed that could move an informed investor's decision, and which those with access may not trade on.

The clauses of a normative instrument that apply across it rather than to one of its chapters. A structural term of the regulation rather than a financial concept, admitted because the corpus uses it as a referent in prose and not only as a section banner.
A share class with a single holder, whose rules are written for that investor alone.

attestation_audit.why: The admission rule is only worth stating if it is applied after the fact as well as before. Every admitted phrase was re-checked against where it actually occurs, because a rule tested only on the candidates you already meant to reject is not a rule. Two entries turned out to sit close to the line and are recorded here rather than left for a reviewer to find.

prose_attested.administrador fiduciário: 3 events in sentences of the conduct chapter

prose_attested.desvio padrão amostral: `Para calcularmos a Variância e o Desvio Padrão Amostral, ao invés de calcular a média…`

attested_by_worked_example_not_by_senten.desvio padrão populacional: The phrase itself is a section title and a figure caption. The CONCEPT is defined under it by full worked example: mean 3%, squared deviations summing to 8, `Variância = 1,6`, `DP = √1,6 = ±1,26`. Dividing by n (8/5 = 1,6) is exactly what makes it populacional, and the sibling amostral section computes 2,00 from the same numbers by dividing by n−1. The corpus distinguishes the two numerically, so the concept is attested even though no sentence contains the phrase. Admitted.
attested_by_worked_example_not_by_senten.valor futuro: Weakest admission in this batch, and flagged as such. The phrase appears once as a section title and once as a table column header — `FLUXO (Valor Futuro)` set against `VALOR PRESENTE`, over the cash flows 60/60/60/60/1.060 that the example discounts at 4 %, 6 % and 8 %. That is the concept in use inside a worked calculation rather than a definition of it, and no sentence defines future value anywhere in the corpus. Kept because a table cell is content and not slide furniture, and because registering the present-value side while refusing its counterpart leaves the dictionary asymmetric on the corpus's own table header. A reviewer who reads `attested only as a column label` and disagrees should remove it — the evidence is here to make that judgement, not to survive it.

refused.RF: 22 occurrences, every one inside a heading, none in a sentence
refused.títulos híbridos: one occurrence, a heading, no prose defining it

known_specificity_loss.título público americano: matches the generic `entity.government_security` where `entity.us_government_security` exists. Not a wrong match — a US Treasury IS a government security — but less specific than the registry can express. Left alone: narrowing it needs a longest-match form for the American variant, which is a separate change with its own measurement.
